faq._note: Tokens in answers are filled from the content above: {opens}, {closes}, {announcement}, {ceremony}, {email}. 'items' shows while nominations.public is false (2026); 'publicItems' shows when public nominations return. Items with confirmed=false are unverified with the client.

publicItems.a: Anyone. Colleagues, neighbours, community members and the people a nominee helped are all welcome to nominate.
The House is confirming whether self-nominations are accepted. Until then, please nominate someone else, or email {email} to ask.

publicItems.q: Does it cost anything to nominate?

publicItems.a: Nominations opened on {opens} and close on {closes}.

publicItems.q: Can I nominate more than one person?
publicItems.a: Yes. Send one form for each nominee.

publicItems.q: Can I nominate a group or an organisation?
publicItems.a: Yes, in the categories that accept them. Community Resilience and Humanitarian Service accept individuals or groups, and National Development is for organisations. Each category shows who is eligible.
About ten minutes. Specific events, places and dates count for more than general praise, so it helps to have those to hand.

publicItems.q: Do I need a link or documents?
publicItems.a: No. A link to news coverage, a letter or photographs helps, but it is optional.

publicItems.q: Will the nominee know I nominated them?
publicItems.a: If your nominee is shortlisted, we contact you, the nominee and one referee to confirm the details. Shortlisted nominees are named publicly only with their consent, and nominees may decline at any time.
Shortlisted claims are verified, then an independent panel from civil society, security, academia and the media scores the shortlist against published criteria. The panel's decision is final.

publicItems.q: When will I hear the outcome?
publicItems.a: Every nominator hears the outcome, shortlisted or not. Honourees are announced on {announcement}.

publicItems.q: I made a mistake in my nomination. What do I do?
publicItems.a: Email {email} with your reference number and the correction.
The Grand Honours on {ceremony} is by invitation. Partners and honourees receive places for their guests.

publicItems.q: How else can I support the programme?
publicItems.a: Organisations can become partners, and anyone can give to support the work.

items.a: Not in this edition. For the first Sentinels of Peace Grand Honours, honourees are selected: our research team identifies candidates across all 36 states and the FCT, and an independent panel chooses the honourees against published criteria.

Our research team identifies candidates and checks each one's record, including with a referee. An independent panel from civil society, security, academia and the media then scores the shortlist against published criteria. The panel's decision is final.
Individuals, groups and organisations whose work prevented conflict, protected lives or helped a community recover, in one of five categories. Each category shows who is eligible.

items.q: Can I apply or put myself forward?
items.a: No. There are no applications in this edition, which keeps the selection independent.

items.q: Does anyone pay to be honoured?
items.a: No. Honourees never pay to be honoured or to attend the ceremony. If anyone asks you for money in the programme's name, they are not from House of Evulv: please report it to {email}.

items.q: Will honourees be asked before they are named?
items.a: Yes. Shortlisted candidates are named publicly only with their consent, and anyone may decline.
Honourees are announced on {announcement}, and presented at the Grand Honours on {ceremony}.
The Grand Honours on {ceremony} is by invitation. Partners and honourees receive places for their guests.

items.q: Will future editions take public nominations?
items.a: If a future edition opens public nominations, we will announce it here.

items.q: How can I support the programme?
items.a: Tell us how you would like to help using the support form on this page. If you represent an organisation, see the partnership tiers.
